response.overview: Camera in hand, camera slung over the shoulder, the photographers and cameramen of the Armies' Film and Photographic Service are present in every operation in Indochina. Raymond Martinoff, Daniel Camus, Lucien Millet, and Pierre Schoendoerffer traverse the rice paddies, the brush, and the jungle alongside the combatants whose actions they are tasked with immortalizing. Yet they are not merely witnesses and even less so journalists but truly soldiers of the image. Their pictures serve to feed the press or newsreels whose goal is to rally the support of a public that remains largely indifferent or hostile to this distant war.
response.title: Filmer la guerre d'Indochine
